newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on weak trade.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on weak trade.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices maintained midday levels to end lower after another weary day of trading without buying interest, dealers said.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted market indicator price for November RSS 1 buyer at 308 cents ($1.23) a kg, down half cent from Monday. November SMR 20 buyer also fell half cent to 304.

Traders quoted the SMR20 at around 304, SMR CV at 362-363, SMR L at 342-343, SMR5 at 310-311, SMR10 at 302-303 and drum latex at 234-235. They said the rebound in Tokyo futures also did not help sentiment.
Traders said producers were, however, showing reluctance to sell at lower levels due to the return of rains, which had restricted rubber tapping and supply of raw materials.
"Supply is already tightening here and in Thailand and producers can always get good prices under this situation if demand returns," said a dealer.

The INRO five-day average fell to 240.41 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 7 from 241.08 on Oct 4. The daily indicator was at 238.41 against 239.72 previously. -- Barani Krishnaan (603-230-7510) ($1=2.5006 ringgit)
